[LDET.3.6.3] **No NaN is written to a floating-point field.** A NaN's sign and
payload are the hardware's ([LEXP.4.3]), so a NaN in a field of a bundle, a
recording or a payload would make its bytes differ by target. Nothing that
writes a message under `proto/` may write a NaN to a `double` or `float` field.
Every such field must have a row in [LDET.3.6.4] naming its writer and the clause
that keeps a NaN out of it, and a field must not be added without one.
